statements.text: Hi! I'm Ingrid, 58, and I've been a cardiology nurse at Haukeland hospital in Bergen for twelve years now.
We rent a third-floor flat in Møhlenpris, no lift, and my knees have opinions about that.
Fjord, our Norwegian elkhound, is seven and still pulls on the lead like a tractor.
I drive a Volkswagen Golf, the old diesel. Dependable, if a bit smelly.
Two cups of strong filter coffee, no milk, and I'm a functioning human by 6am.
Phone situation: iPhone 12, and the battery is flat by mid-afternoon.
Learning Italian on Duolingo, ten minutes at lunch, because Arne and I booked Puglia for April.
My GP put me on atorvastatin after the cholesterol numbers came back ugly.
In the evenings I knit, mostly socks. Right now it's a dark green pair for my sister Solveig.
Kjersti is my ward manager and she's been very decent about letting me swap shifts.
We brought home a rescue dachshund on Saturday! Her name is Pølse and she is roughly the size of a loaf of bread.
Swapped the Golf for a used Nissan Leaf last week. Hello, silent commuting.
Funny detail about the Leaf, it's the 40 kWh one in pearl white, good for about 250 km in summer.
Arne gave me an iPhone 15 for my birthday and the battery lasts a whole day. Feels like cheating.
Henrik started on the ward this week as the new manager. Very orderly man, loves a spreadsheet.
My sister Solveig has been a librarian in Trondheim since 2010.
Back from Puglia! Orecchiette every single day, and I actually ordered dinner in Italian without anyone switching to English.
Arne has decided to learn Italian too, he's on Babbel and quotes phrases at breakfast.
Deleted Duolingo. I have a weekly Zoom lesson with a tutor called Giulia now and it's miles better.
We've moved! Ground-floor flat in Fana with a little garden. No more stairs, thank God.
Muscle aches on the atorvastatin, so the GP switched me to rosuvastatin.
Dropped to 60% at work so I get proper weekdays at home.
Started swimming at Sartor pool on Tuesday mornings, a slow kilometre.
Coffee's out. Night shifts made my heart race, so it's peppermint tea now.
Bloodwork looks great, so I'm off statins entirely, doctor's orders.
The new rota killed Tuesdays, so swimming has moved to Wednesday evenings.
Also took up watercolours, a beginner course on Mondays. My seagulls look like potatoes.

statements.text: Hey, it's Kofi. Just landed in Toronto to start my master's in civil engineering at U of T. It's September and already freezing, how.
I'm renting a room in a shared house near Kensington Market with two roommates, Dev and Marcus.
My laptop is a ThinkPad T14 that my brother Yaw handed down to me. Keyboard's great, battery isn't.
Getting to campus means the 506 streetcar, about 35 minutes if it doesn't get stuck behind a delivery truck.
I'm on a Samsung Galaxy A54. Nothing fancy, does the job.
Sundays I play pickup football at Christie Pits with a bunch of Ghanaians and Brazilians.
Learned I'm allergic to shellfish at a wedding in Mississauga. Not recommended, one star.
Spotify is basically my entire day, Afrobeats playlist on loop while I study.
Got the TA gig for the structural analysis course, ten hours a week of marking and office hours.
My thesis supervisor is Dr. Okafor, super sharp, replies to emails at 2am.
The thesis is on monitoring fatigue in old bridges using cheap accelerometers.
Left the Kensington house, I've got a one-bedroom of my own in North York near Finch station now.
Subway all the way now, Line 1 from Finch. It's an hour each way but at least I can read.
Dropped my phone in the lake at Cherry Beach, so I bought a Pixel 8a on Saturday.
Yaw just started at a fintech in Accra, he's a backend developer there now.
Signed up for a French evening class on Wednesdays at the community centre, half the job postings here ask for it.
The ThinkPad finally died, so I picked up a refurbished MacBook Air M2 for nine hundred bucks.
The MacBook has 16 GB of RAM, plenty for my finite element runs.
Done with TAing, I start a four-month internship at Brightline Engineering on Monday.
Found out I'm allergic to peanuts too, courtesy of a satay skewer. EpiPen lives in my bag now.
Switched to Apple Music, the new Mac came with six free months.
Dr. Okafor is going on sabbatical, so Dr. Lindqvist takes over as my supervisor.
Also dabbling in Portuguese with the Brazilians after football, mostly swear words so far.
My girlfriend Esi is doing her nursing degree at Humber.
Ran my first 10k along the waterfront, 58 minutes and I nearly died at the finish.
Football is on Saturday mornings now, Sundays belong to my long run.
Bought a used Trek last week, so I bike to campus now instead of taking the train, forty minutes along the Don trail.

statements.text: Mateo here. I run a little taquería in Monterrey, La Esquina de Don Chato. Six years open this August.
Our house is in Colonia Mitras Centro, a ten-minute drive from the restaurant.
My work truck is a 2015 Ford Ranger, red, 190,000 km and still refusing to die.
Tango, our beagle, ate an entire tray of al pastor off the counter yesterday. Zero remorse.
Beto is my head cook, he's been with me since day one and I honestly can't picture the place without him.
Valentina turned nine today and announced she's going to be a vet.
Doctor has me on losartan for my blood pressure, one pill every morning.
Morning coffee is café de olla with piloncillo, my mom's recipe, the only way.
My phone is a Motorola Moto G Power and the screen is cracked in two places.
Cards at the counter go through our Clip terminal.
Trying to learn English on Babbel, fifteen minutes before bed, for all the tourists who come in after Rayados games.
Weekends I escape to Presa de la Boca to fish with my brother-in-law Ramiro.
CrossFit at 6am, Monday Wednesday Friday. My wife says I've become insufferable.
Santiago lost his first tooth tonight and the tooth fairy paid in pesos, naturally.
Beto left for a hotel kitchen in San Pedro, so Chuy has taken over as head cook at the taquería.
Sold the Ranger to my cousin and bought a used 2019 Toyota Hilux.
The Hilux is the white double-cab, automatic, and the AC actually works. Luxury.
Lucía's manager at the bank, Mrs. Treviño, keeps scheduling meetings at 5pm on Fridays.
Switched from losartan to amlodipine, the losartan gave me a dry cough.
We got a second dog! A rescue greyhound mix called Chispa, skinny as a broom.
Shot the new menu photos with my iPhone 13 and honestly the camera is stunning.
Mercado Pago terminals replaced Clip at the counter this week, the fees are lower.
Doctor wants less sugar, so it's plain black Americano now. I miss the piloncillo.
We moved to a bigger house in Cumbres, finally a proper yard for the dogs.
Signed a lease on a second location in Guadalupe, opening in September. Terrified.
Quit CrossFit after my knee started complaining, I do laps at the municipal pool now.
The iPhone took a swim in a pot of frijoles, so I'm on a Galaxy S24 FE now, and I secretly prefer it.
Hired Pepe to be head cook at the Guadalupe place when it opens.
